decisions.rationale: airport_id (bronze id) has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 9057 equal to row_count 9057, so it uniquely identifies every row; ident and iata_code show the same cardinality and could serve as alternates, but the numeric id is the stable surrogate key.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 9057, so no deduplication step is applied and dedupe_strategy is none.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata and carry no business meaning (_airbyte_meta is uniformly '{}'); all three are dropped.
scheduled_service has exactly 2 distinct values ('yes', 'no') with null_rate 0.0, so it is mapped deterministically to BOOLEAN as has_scheduled_service.
All id samples are integral digit strings and the column is fully populated, so the landed VARCHAR is cast to INTEGER; a failed cast at build time would signal a source regression.

latitude_deg and longitude_deg landed as DECIMAL(38,9) but samples show at most 6 decimal places within valid geographic ranges (lat -79.777778 to 82.517263, lon -179.876999 to 179.9757), so they are narrowed to DECIMAL(9,6) and DECIMAL(10,6); elevation_ft samples are all integral and are cast to INTEGER.
local_code (null_rate 0.636635), keywords (0.679585), and home_link (0.749034) are sparsely populated but retained as nullable columns; no rows are dropped and no values are imputed.

purpose: silver_ourairports_airports is the cleaned reference table of world airports from the OurAirports bronze feed: one row per airport with its identifiers (airport_id, ident, iata_code, icao_code, gps_code, local_code), classification (airport_type, has_scheduled_service), location (latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation_ft, continent, iso_country, iso_region, municipality), and reference links. It feeds downstream geographic enrichment, route analysis, and airport dimension builds.
usage: Join on airport_id as the primary key; ident and iata_code are also fully populated and unique in this snapshot and may serve as natural-key joins, but only airport_id is contractually the grain. has_scheduled_service is a true/false boolean derived from the source's yes/no text. Consumers needing icao_code, gps_code, local_code, municipality, home_link, wikipedia_link, elevation_ft, or keywords must handle nulls explicitly, as these columns are nullable and nulls are retained as-is.
limitations: Several columns are sparsely populated and were retained without imputation: local_code is 63.7% null, keywords is 68.0% null, and home_link is 74.9% null; icao_code is 13.7% null and elevation_ft is 3.7% null. The keywords column is unparsed free text that mixes alternate codes and names. Coordinate precision is capped at six decimal places by the cast from DECIMAL(38,9). No cross-field geographic validation (e.g. country/region consistency) was performed in this cleanup.
